title: Digital Growth Readiness Score
subtitle: Measures how ready your business is to grow through digital marketing — before you invest a rupee in ads.

questions.text: When a potential client searches for your business online right now, what do they find?

answers.label: Nothing — no website, no active social profiles
An outdated or broken website, or a social page that hasn't been updated in months
A working website and some profiles, but nothing that builds immediate trust
A professional website with results or testimonials and an active social presence
A complete digital presence with clear proof, reviews, and content that earns trust before any conversation happens

questions.text: How would you describe your business's LinkedIn presence today?

answers.label: No LinkedIn page or profile for the business at all
Profile exists but hasn't been posted to or updated in months
Active occasionally, but no consistent posting or meaningful engagement
Posting regularly with growing engagement from the right type of audience
LinkedIn is a consistent source of warm leads and credibility for the business

questions.text: How much does a prospect already trust your business before they speak to you for the first time?

answers.label: Not at all — they only reach out because someone they know personally referred them
Slightly — they've heard the name but can't verify your work anywhere online
Somewhat — they've found a website but haven't seen real proof of results
Fairly — they've read your content or seen client results before reaching out
Strongly — your digital presence does most of the trust-building long before the first call

low.headline: Your foundation is the gap — not your ads
low.text: In my outreach work I've met manufacturing businesses with decades of experience and genuinely great products that are operating with almost no online presence. Prospects can't trust what they can't find. Digital marketing isn't just about running Meta Ads or Google Ads — before investing in advertising, you need a foundation that makes potential customers trust you. Build that first.
steps: Get a clean, working website live — this is the non-negotiable starting point for everything else
Complete your LinkedIn company page with a clear description of exactly who you help and what outcome you deliver
Collect 3 to 5 client testimonials or case study snapshots and make them easy to find before anyone has to ask

mid.headline: You're online — but your presence isn't doing the trust-building work yet
mid.text: Having a website and some active profiles already puts you ahead of more businesses than you'd expect. The next step is making sure those assets are actually building confidence in a prospect before they reach out — not just confirming that you exist.
steps: Audit your website — does it show specific results, or just describe services in general terms?
Post on LinkedIn at least 3 times a week with real lessons from your client work — not announcements
Add at least one specific case study or client result to your website and LinkedIn profile this week

high.headline: Your foundation is solid — now amplify it with paid traffic
high.text: You've built the kind of digital presence that earns trust before anyone speaks to you. That's rarer than you'd think. The opportunity now is driving paid traffic to that foundation and making sure your conversion system captures every interested prospect who arrives.
steps: Test a small paid campaign pointing directly to your strongest proof page or case study
Set up retargeting so prospects who've visited your site see a relevant follow-up offer
Review your analytics monthly — find where visitors are dropping off and fix that before increasing spend

questions.text: If someone asked what your business does in one sentence, how clear would your answer be?

answers.label: We do many things — the answer depends on who's asking
I can explain it but it usually takes a few minutes and a lot of context
I have a rough one-liner but it doesn't always land the way I want
We have one clear sentence that most people understand immediately
Our one-liner is specific enough that prospects often say 'that's exactly what I've been looking for'

questions.text: How would you describe the type of business you work with?

answers.label: Any business that needs marketing help — we don't turn work away based on industry
A few different industries with no clear pattern between them
Mostly one or two types of business but we haven't formally committed to them
A specific type of business and we've actively turned down work that falls outside that focus
A clearly defined audience — our positioning, content, and outreach all reflect that single choice

questions.text: When a campaign isn't performing, what is your first instinct?

answers.label: Adjust the targeting, change the creative, or increase the budget — and keep running
Pause the campaign and wait to see if results improve on their own
Look at the landing page and test a few changes there
Check whether the offer itself is compelling before touching anything in the campaign
Run a structured diagnosis — offer, audience, creative, landing page, timing — and fix the actual root cause

questions.text: How often do prospects push back on your price before you've had a chance to explain your offer properly?

answers.label: Almost every conversation — price is the first and biggest objection
Frequently — we often have to discount to close
Sometimes — but we can usually justify the value if given the chance
Rarely — the offer communicates the return clearly enough that price rarely comes up first
Almost never — by the time prospects reach us, they already understand the value

low.headline: The problem probably isn't your ads
low.text: After working with different businesses across industries, one thing has become very clear to me: performance marketing can only amplify a good offer. It cannot make a weak or unclear offer look attractive. Before you change your targeting or increase your budget, get your offer sharper. That one shift changes everything downstream.
steps: Write down the single specific problem you solve and exactly who you solve it for — if it takes more than two sentences, keep cutting
Ask your last three clients what made them choose you — their words are almost always clearer than the language you've been using
Remove anything from your pitch that doesn't directly connect to that one specific problem

mid.headline: You're getting clearer — now commit to it fully
mid.text: You've started building clarity around your offer, but there's still some hedging. The businesses that grow fastest are the ones brave enough to say 'this is exactly what I do' and stop trying to appeal to everyone. Removing distractions is not the same as losing opportunity — it's often how you create it.
steps: Pick your one strongest service and lead with it in every conversation, proposal, and piece of content
Rewrite your website headline to name a specific outcome, not a service category
Test your one-liner with five prospects this week and watch whether they understand it immediately without follow-up explanation

high.headline: Your offer is doing the selling — now let ads do the reaching
high.text: A clear, compelling offer is what everything else is built on. You've got that. When campaigns underperform now, you know to look at the system — not doubt the offer. That's a significant advantage over most businesses running paid traffic.
steps: Document your offer framework so any future team member can explain it the same way you would
Build one strong case study around your best client result and use it as the anchor in your ad creatives
Set a standing rule: before changing any campaign element, confirm the offer has been clearly communicated first

questions.text: What happens the moment someone shows interest in your business — fills in a form, clicks a contact button, or sends a message?

answers.label: Nothing automated — we wait for them to call back or find us again
They get a generic auto-reply and someone follows up manually when we notice it
We follow up within a day or two with a call or email
We have an automated sequence that responds within an hour and starts qualifying them
We have a system that captures, qualifies, follows up, and books a call — usually within minutes

questions.text: How clearly can you trace which specific marketing activity brought in your last paying client?

answers.label: We can't — most clients come through word-of-mouth and we don't know the exact source
We ask informally but don't record or analyse the answer
We use basic platform reporting but can't connect it to actual revenue
We track leads from source to close and know our rough cost per client
We have full visibility — lead source, stage conversion rates, and cost per acquisition every month

questions.text: How deliberate are you about showing your offer at the exact moment a prospect is most likely to say yes?

answers.label: We present our offer the same way to everyone regardless of where they are in their buying process
We occasionally follow up after events or content but there's no real structure to it
We have some follow-up in place but timing is not a deliberate part of the strategy
We time outreach to high-intent moments — after content downloads, events, or specific page visits
Our system automatically identifies high-intent moments and presents the right offer at that exact point

low.headline: Most of your interested prospects are going cold before you reach them
low.text: Good marketing is not just about showing the right offer — it's about showing the offer at the right moment, and having a system ready to catch the interest before it fades. Right now, every person who's visited your site or seen your content and done nothing is a potential client who left because there was no clear next step waiting for them.
steps: Set up a simple contact form connected to an instant email notification — so you know the second someone raises their hand
Write one follow-up message template you can send within two hours of any new enquiry
Add one tracking link to your most important page so you can see how many people are arriving but not converting

mid.headline: You're catching some leads — but missing the high-intent window
mid.text: You have the basics in place. The gap is speed and automation. When someone has just read your content or visited your pricing page, that's the moment they're most likely to say yes. If your follow-up takes 24 hours, that window has usually already closed.
steps: Set up an automated response that goes out within 15 minutes of any form submission — not hours
Add retargeting to your ad accounts so people who've visited your site see a relevant follow-up offer
Review your last 10 enquiries — how long did it take you to respond, and how many of those actually converted?

high.headline: Your system catches leads — now find and close the gaps
high.text: You've built what most businesses are still missing: a system that works even when you're not watching. Now the work is identifying exactly where prospects are still slipping through and tightening those points.
steps: Map your full funnel on paper — find the stage where the highest percentage of prospects drop off
Test your follow-up timing — try responding in 5 minutes versus 30 and measure which converts at a higher rate
Build a monthly review habit: source, stage conversion rate, and cost per acquisition — compare month on month

questions.text: Before launching a Meta Ads or Google Ads campaign, how do you typically prepare?

answers.label: Set a budget and launch — figure out what works as we go
Do some audience research and set up basic targeting before going live
Build a landing page, set up basic tracking, and define a target audience
Validate the offer, set up conversion tracking, prepare the landing page, and define a target cost per lead before any spend goes live
Run a full readiness check — offer, audience, creative, landing page, tracking, and a clear test hypothesis — before the first rupee is spent

questions.text: How do you decide whether an ad campaign is actually working?

answers.label: We look at clicks, reach, and likes and judge from there
We use the platform's reported results and make decisions based on what it shows us
We track leads generated and follow up manually to see how many became paying clients
We track cost per lead and cost per acquisition and compare both against our targets
We trace the full path from ad spend to revenue and know our exact return on every campaign

questions.text: How many hours per week does your team (or you personally) spend on manual outreach and lead follow-up with no automation?
questions.hint: Include cold calls, manual DMs, email chasing, and manual check-ins. Do not include ad management or strategy time.

low.headline: Spending on ads before fixing the system is the most expensive mistake in performance marketing
low.text: Running paid traffic without clear tracking, a validated offer, and a conversion system in place is like filling a bucket with holes — the budget disappears, results are unclear, and the instinct is to blame the targeting or the platform. Fix the system first. Every time.
steps: Set up conversion tracking in Google or Meta before spending another rupee — without this, every campaign decision is a guess
Define what a successful campaign looks like in numbers before you launch: how much can you spend per lead and still be profitable?
Run one small test campaign with a tight budget, one audience, one offer, and measure only cost per lead — nothing else for the first run

mid.headline: You're tracking — now connect what you're tracking to actual revenue
mid.text: You're ahead of most businesses that run ads. The next step is closing the loop between campaign metrics and what actually lands in the bank. Do you know which campaign last month brought in a paying client, and what that client was worth to the business?
steps: Add UTM parameters to every ad so you can trace a lead all the way back to the exact campaign and creative that generated it
Set up a simple CRM or even a spreadsheet that records every lead from source to closed or lost
Calculate your true cost per acquisition this month — not just cost per lead

high.headline: You think in systems, not just campaigns — that's the real skill in performance marketing
high.text: Most business owners think performance marketing is about running good ads. You already know it's about building a system where every rupee spent is traceable to a result. That clarity is what lets you scale without guessing.
steps: Document your campaign launch process so any future team member follows the same pre-launch checklist
Test one new audience segment or creative format each month with a clear hypothesis before you start
Run a monthly budget review: if cost per acquisition is within your target, increase spend — if not, diagnose before you scale

cta.headline: Want a partner who turns this score into an actual plan?
cta.description: Most people don't fail at the assessment. They fail at sequencing. In 30 minutes I'll show you which two things to fix first, based on your score and your stage. No pitch deck, just the sequencing call.

computed_outputs.label: Hours spent on manual outreach per year at your current pace

persona_selector.text: Which best describes where your business gets most of its new clients right now?

answers.label: Almost entirely offline — referrals, word-of-mouth, direct networking
A mix of offline and digital, but no clear system in place
Running ads already but results are inconsistent or hard to explain
Growing digitally and looking to scale faster and more predictably
